Great game. It's easy to pick up and complete, and it's not overly long, so the hacking never gets to the point of feeling like a chore. One of the most interesting things to do is going through all files in every computer you hack to find snippets of hilarity, like dorky, chat-based jokes, or why you should gift potatoes instead of roses to the one you love. There are all sorts of missions, including some that manage to make you ponder about some sensitive subjects. There's also some meta-gaming, with you having to use your actual computer's command prompt to clear a section. All in all, quite a pleasant experience. Recommended

This is an awesome game. It's unique. I love how the game breaks down hacking and separates it into stages. This gives you that feeling like you ARE actually hacking someone's computer. Flooding proxy servers with useless info to override them, checking personal emails, checking text files, copying important files to your computer, there is a good amount of detail. It also takes patience/practice. You will definitely get frustrated, but it's a fun challenge. I feel you can also learn a little bit about how certain things work on a computer, too, just as side note. All in all, I highly recommend this game! This is meant for any age and any type of gamer.

I know next to nothing about coding. I just have this fascination with cybersecurity and hacking. Like, maybe an unhealthy fascination after reading books like Sandworm, Spam Nation, and Countdown to Zero Day, as well as watching shows like Mr. Robot. Anyway, I figured I'd give this game a shot.

I immediately fell in love with the game play. It starts out fairly easy with some decent challenges, and then manages to scale pretty well to continuously give you the sense that you can accomplish things, but it takes a bit of thought power. The story was also well written, and really helped the game play along. It added a real sense of being a digital detective. Additionally, though the game is mostly text based, the visuals they do have are well done, especially with the .exe files. The music was also really well done and compiled from some really solid artists in the electronic/synthwave genres. Lastly, there's a ton of little details, some easter eggs, and fun nuanced concepts that just make the game more immersive. I believe I played 17 hours, and that felt like it flew by.

Anyway, like I said, I don't know much of anything about coding, but by the end of the game I felt really competent in the game play. I can't wait for more DLC and maybe the sequel!

I really really loved this. I've played casual hacking games for many years and this one hits just in the right spot. 

A fair warning though: if you know nothing about code lines or are really really bad at it, you're going to have a hard time. I'm somewhat savvy and still struggled for the first few levels. The game does NOT hold your hand, even if all of the tools and knowledge you need to progress are right there. It was particularly tough picking the game back up after a few weeks. The commands were just gone from my mind. And then just as I got REALLY into it, poof, it was over. Labyrinths was also excellent and very similar, yet different enough that it felt fresh.

Just as other players' comments, this is a really awesome game. I really enjoy playing this game and I would like to recommend this game to others. But I am facing some issues recently.

 I bought an M1 MacBook Pro, I am not sure it is caused by M1 or MacOS itself, the game often freezes, and the only way to solve this is to force quit then restart the game. And there are other bugs when playing under MacOS. All the webpages inside the game such as the CFC chicken webpage, they just won't display, it is either showing "loading" and the spinning flower-like logo, or showing blank. 

And for some reasons, this game seems to be running a bit more efficient under Windows than under MacOS. When running under MacOS Big Sur, I am getting 60fps, and the SoC temperature is already around 80C or more, sometime the game feels a bit laggy. It uses almost 100% of my M1 GPU  processing power. But when running on the same computer under Windows through Parallels Desktop, I am getting 120 fps and the machine is relatively cooler. the M1 SoC temperature is around 60-70C. Moreover, all the stability and display issues mentioned previously has never appeared under parallels desktop, at least not yet. 

In addition, the gaming profiles seems to be not compatible over different platforms. The gaming record created on my old PC before I swapped to M1 just won't load on the M1 Mac, no matter I am running the game under Windows in ParallelsDesktop or directly under MacOS. Same happens to two Operating Systems on M1. Records created under MacOS will not load under Windows in PD, and records created under Windows in PD also won't load under MacOS.

Fun and captivating - the 3hs on log at time of writing are all from one sitting haha. I can't say every game captivates me like that. Interface is simple, and there is a bit of a learning curve. Reading more than you're strictly required can help you become more competent at manipulating the game's commands, which is really a lot of what the game relies on. I feel it walks the line between being a fun video game and actually simulating interacting with computer programming very well.

So far my only complaint is that it feels like I was starting to grind missions, but honestly I've been sitting here playing for 3 hours and I'm sure I'll be back on next time I have some free time, and it'll be nice to be able to just mess around and fill some contracts before the plot picks back up.

Put simply, Hacknet is one of the first games I actually bought the DLC for. 

Hacknet has an immersive story, well done soundtrack, and it can feel like you're actually hacking into someones. With hidden features (IE The "TRUE ULTIMATE POWER" achievement) and storylines developed by the community I'd definitely recommend this game to people interested in hacking/coding.

I was so addicted, I played and completed this over 3 days - and if real life hadn't got in the way I'd have sat and completed it in one go!

The pacing of the game is spot on, gradually providing you with new tools and new skills as the difficulty level slowly increase and the sense of achievement when you a complete a mission is real. Sure, all the missions broadly boil down to the same thing (hack a server, steal, delete or amend files and get out), but, narrative driven as they are, they never feel repetitive.

Hacknet is one of the best purchases I have recently made. This game is a hacking simulator that doesn't feel too cheesy- it falls right between Hollywood-style badass hacking and realism. While it may seem intimidating at first, Hacknet is easy to pick up, but will still actively challenge the player with new and unique missions with solutions that any player can reach without help. The story for this game is pretty good- I do have to say, I enjoyed the DLC (Labyrinths) story far more, but that was likely due to the fact that I felt more involved with a team. Nonetheless, Hacknet is a masterpiece that you should definitely buy. The DLC is very cheap, and it's more of a whole new game than a DLC. Please consider putting Hacknet in your library, I promise you won't regret it.

P.S. you get to put in the name you are referred to so you can use a badass hacker alias 10/10

I've never played anything like Hacknet so I'm loving the unique (to me) and exciting experience so far.
